To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned a testis-specific form of calpastatin that is localized to the sperm membrane and may play a role in the calcium-mediated sperm acrosome reaction.
the human tCAST protein has a different domain structure than human sCAST, and tCAST is present in human sperm and in human testes.
we have identified a testis-specific calpastatin isoform, which is a potential target for sperm-agglutination antibodies in infertile patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of sperm antigens that may have a role in the immunopathogenesis of infertility.
the identification of a human sperm-specific calpastatin isoform, which may be involved in the sperm acrosomal reaction.
the identification and functional characterization of the sperm-specific isoform of the endogenous calpain inhibitor, calpastatin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tCAST has a unique domain structure and may have a unique biological function.
the testis isoform of calpain inhibitor (tCAST) is the first example of a testis-specific protein isoform that is generated by alternative splicing of a gene.
tCAST is the first testis-specific protein isoform of calpain inhibitor to be identified and cloned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the testis-specific calpastatin (TCAST) is a novel calpastatin isoform that differs from the somatic form in domain structure and subcellular distribution.
the T domain of tCAST is a novel protein domain that targets the cytoplasm and the membrane, whereas the N domain of sCAST is responsible for the nuclear localization of calpastatin.
tCAST is an alternative splice variant of the calpastain gene that is expressed in human testis and sperm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified a testis-specific form of calpastatin and demonstrated that it is present in the human testes and human sperm.
the T domain of human tCAST is sufficient for membrane association and may be important for the localization of calpastatin at sites of calcium-mediated membrane fusion events.
the testis-specific isoforms of calpastatin may have a role in sperm function.
